patients.summary: High school math teacher in Easthampton who joined the practice well in 2022. Spells in autumn 2024 led to a right adrenal pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid carcinoma from MEN 2A (RET p.Cys634Arg); right adrenalectomy 2025-11-14 and total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection 2026-01-22. Now on levothyroxine with calcitonin, CEA and yearly metanephrine surveillance.

events.reason: New patient visit to establish primary care

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
43 y/o woman establishing care. Left her old practice when her doctor retired; records release signed at check-in. Feels well, no complaints today. Teaches high school math, school year starts in two weeks.

PMH: none. She has never been on a daily medication.
PSH: tonsillectomy 1995 (age 16); cesarean section 2015.
Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother with high blood pressure. Father died in his 40s; she was told it was "a thyroid problem" and has never seen any records.
Social: never smoker. 1-2 drinks a week, socially. No drug use. Lives in Easthampton.
Prevention per pt: Pap and mammogram at prior office, both normal as far as she knows (will confirm on records). Has never had colon screening. Cannot remember her last tetanus shot. COVID primary series plus one booster elsewhere.

ROS: negative in full - no fatigue, palpitations, headaches, bowel change or weight change.

Objective
BP 115/72, HR 73 /min, SpO2 98 %, T 37.0 C
Wt 64.0 kg, Ht 165.7 cm, BMI 23.3 kg/m2
Well appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: TMs and oropharynx normal, tonsils surgically absent.
Neck: supple, thyroid not enlarged, no adenopathy.
CV: RRR, S1/S2 normal, no murmurs.
Lungs: clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender, well-healed low transverse scar.
Ext: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions.
Psych: normal mood and affect.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

Assessment/Plan
Healthy 43F, new to us. No chronic problems.
- Screening labs today: CBC, BMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees.
- Tdap given today (last unknown).
- Screening mammogram ordered.
- Cervical screening: confirm date of last co-test from records.
- Colon screening due at 45; will discuss next year.
- Flu and the updated COVID booster this fall.
- RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Melissa,
All of your labs from yesterday came back normal. Blood counts, kidney function, electrolytes and blood sugar are fine. Cholesterol is in a good range (LDL 95 mg/dL, HDL 60 mg/dL). HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and neither needs repeating unless something changes.
Nice to meet you, and good luck with the start of the school year.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care practice

documents.title: Prior practice records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from pt's previous primary care office, 38 pages. Scanned to media.

Abstracted for chart:
- Problem list at prior office: none.
- Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test 06/2018: NILM, HPV negative.
- Screening mammogram 10/2021: BI-RADS 1, negative.
- Immunizations: Tdap 05/2011. Pfizer COVID 03/2021, 04/2021, booster 11/2021.
- Labs 2021: CBC, CMP and lipids, all unremarkable.
Immunization history entered. Forwarded to PCP for review.

PCP addendum: reviewed. Co-test due 2023. Good to have the 2011 Tdap date - this year's dose was appropriate.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here after school for flu shot and bivalent COVID booster. Feeling well, no fever. Screening questions negative, NKDA.
Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Pfizer bivalent 0.3 mL IM R deltoid.
VIS sheets given. Waited 15 min in the lobby without any problem. Expect a sore arm, may take acetaminophen if needed.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: 10/2021 outside study. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion in either breast. No change from prior.

documents.title: Form for school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the district is updating staff files and asked everyone to have a doctor sign the attached employee health form by the end of June. It just needs a signature that I'm under a doctor's care and fit for work, nothing else. Can I drop it off or should I upload it here? Thank you!

documents.title: RE: Form for school
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Hi Melissa, uploading it here is perfect, thank you. We got it and it's in your doctor's box. Forms take up to 5 business days and we'll message you when it's ready to pick up or we can fax it straight to the district if you send the number.
PCP signed 6/2 - faxed to district office per pt request.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation, transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV DNA: not detected.

orders.reason: Colorectal cancer screening, average risk, age 45 in November

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: yearly physical. Doing well, no new concerns. Summer was quiet, back in the classroom next week.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. No change in family or social hx. Never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk.
ROS: negative.

Vitals: BP 115/70, HR 81 /min, RR 17 /min, SpO2 97 %, Wt 63.3 kg.
Gen: well, NAD.
Neck: supple, thyroid normal size, no nodes.
Heart: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Breasts: deferred to imaging per pt preference.
Abd: benign.
Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix appears normal; co-test collected.
Ext: no edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P - adult wellness exam, 44F
1. Cervical screening: Pap with HPV collected today (last 2018).
2. Colon cancer screening: turns 45 in November. Prefers colonoscopy over stool testing. GI referral placed so she can schedule over a school break.
3. Mammogram: last 11/2022. Ordered for this winter.
4. Labs: CBC, BMP.
5. Flu and updated COVID vaccine this fall - she usually goes to the pharmacy.
Next physical 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Melissa - your Pap test is normal and the HPV test is negative. With that combination you won't need another one for five years (2028). The blood work from last week was also all normal (hemoglobin 13.6 g/dL, creatinine 0.64 mg/dL). GI should be calling you about scheduling the colonoscopy. Have a good start to the year.

documents.title: Outside immunizations reconciled
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State immunization registry shows flu vaccine and 2023-2024 Pfizer COVID vaccine given 10/21/2023 at a community pharmacy. Added to immunization history. Health maintenance updated.
